summary: evals/ may now import nora.domain -- S5's render_transcript_at reaches nora.domain.blocks.render_messages/nora.domain.models directly, which the layered-import contract (both the import-linter contract and its AST-based test backstop) correctly caught as a boundary violation.
details: nora/domain/__init__.py's own docstring: "framework-free contracts, imports only the standard library" -- pure types and pure functions, not a collaborator or an assembly seam, so allowing it does not reopen the "no caller assembles a Nora" property nora.subject exists to hold (the same reasoning that let nora.subject itself join this allowlist on 2026-09-17).

Updated both enforcement points: pyproject.toml's "evals may only reach nora.app, nora.testing and nora.subject" import-linter contract (renamed, nora.domain removed from forbidden_modules) and tests/test_boundaries.py's EVALS_ALLOWED_NORA_PACKAGES AST-based backstop.
Found by the full test suite (tests/test_boundaries.py::test_evals_only_imports_nora_app_and_nora_testing), not missed silently -- both enforcement mechanisms did their job.
